summary: In a distributed data store, you can only pick two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance. Under network partitions (P), choose Consistency (CP) or Availability (AP). PACELC extends this: Else (no partition), choose Latency (L) or Consistency (C).
tradeoffs: CP: Strong consistency, rejects writes on partition (e.g., ZooKeeper, Google Spanner, HBase). AP: High availability, eventual consistency (e.g., DynamoDB, Cassandra, CouchDB).
rules_of_thumb: Financial/transactions favor CP. Social feeds, chat status, telemetry favor AP.

summary: Strategies for caching data in Redis/Memcached to accelerate read-heavy applications.

patterns.Cache-Aside: App queries cache; on miss, reads DB, writes to cache. Most popular, resilient to cache failures.
patterns.Write-Through: App writes to cache; cache synchronously writes to DB. High consistency, higher write latency.
patterns.Write-Behind (Write-Back): App writes to cache; cache asynchronously batches writes to DB. Ultra-fast writes, risk of data loss on cache crash.

eviction_policies: LRU (Least Recently Used), LFU (Least Frequently Used), FIFO, TTL expiration.

summary: Techniques for scaling database layers from thousands to millions of operations per second.

strategies.Read Replicas: Primary accepts writes, replicates to read-only replicas. Ideal for 90:10 read:write ratios.
strategies.Horizontal Sharding: Partitions data across multiple database instances by shard key (e.g., user_id % N or hash range).
strategies.Federation (Functional Partitioning): Splits databases by business domain (Users DB, Payments DB, Orders DB).

gotchas: Cross-shard joins are expensive and require denormalization or application-layer aggregation.
